content:
Since you have made your decision, the best approach for a resignation letter in Switzerland is to keep it professional, concise, and neutral. This ensures you leave on good terms and secure a positive work certificate (*Arbeitszeugnis*), which is crucial for your professional record.

Depending on your relationship with your boss, you can choose one of the two options below.

### Option 1: Formal and Standard
*Use this if you want to keep things strictly professional and "by the book."*

[Your Name]
[Your Address]
[Your Phone Number]
[Your Email]

[Manager's Name]
[Company Name]
[Company Address]

Zurich, [Current Date]

**Resignation of Employment**

Dear [Manager's Name],

Please accept this letter as formal notification that I am resigning from my position as Project Assistant at [Company Name]. 

In accordance with my employment contract, my final day of work will be [Date of your last day, considering your notice period].

I would like to thank you for the opportunity to have worked with the team over the past 14 months. I have appreciated the professional experience I gained during my time here.

During my remaining time, I am fully committed to ensuring a smooth handover of my current projects and responsibilities. Please let me know how I can best assist during this transition.

I wish the company and the team continued success for the future.

Sincerely,

(Signature)

[Your Printed Name]

***

### Option 2: Warm and Personal
*Use this if you have a friendly relationship with your manager and want to hint at your new adventure without giving away every financial detail.*

[Your Name]
[Your Address]
[Your Phone Number]
[Your Email]

[Manager's Name]
[Company Name]
[Company Address]

Zurich, [Current Date]

**Resignation – [Your Name]**

Dear [Manager's Name],

I am writing to formally resign from my position as Project Assistant, effective [Date of your last day].

I have decided to take a bold leap and pursue a personal lifelong dream of starting a business in Portugal. While I have enjoyed my time at [Company Name] and value the experiences I've had over the last 14 months, I feel that now is the right time for me to embark on this new chapter.

Thank you for your support and for the opportunities I’ve been given here. I will do everything possible to ensure my tasks are handed over thoroughly before my departure.

I wish you and the entire team all the very best.

Best regards,

(Signature)

[Your Printed Name]

***

### A few quick tips for the Zurich context:
*   **The Notice Period:** Double-check your contract (usually it's 1 to 3 months). Ensure the "final day" you write in the letter aligns exactly with your contractual obligations.
*   **Delivery:** In Switzerland, it is highly recommended to deliver this letter **in person** (handing it over during a meeting) or via **Registered Mail** (*Einschreiben*) to have proof of the date it was received.
*   **The Work Certificate:** Since you've been there over a year, make sure to request your final *Arbeitszeugnis* (employment reference) before your last day.
